svg.aria-label: Five cache invalidation methods shown on the same cached table: purge deletes rows, refresh replaces them, ban marks them invalid, TTL lets them expire, and stale-while-revalidate serves them while refetching
svg.text: Cache invalidation methods, each applied to the same cached table
Purge: remove the cached rows for Alice at once
The next request for Alice goes to the
origin, and the fresh copy is stored.
Refresh: fetch the latest data for Ahmad, even though a copy is cached
Nothing is removed. The cached rows are
Ban: mark the rows for Alice as invalid, without deleting them
The rows stay in memory but are never
served. The next request for Alice fetches
Time-to-live (TTL): the rows for Ahmad expire 2 minutes after they were cached
When the timer runs out the rows count
as stale. The next request fetches them
Stale-while-revalidate: serve the cached rows now, update them in the background
The user gets the cached rows at once.
A background fetch brings the latest
green: new data from the origin
